newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 21.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
MOVE TO RESOLVE POLITICAL IMPASSE IN UTTAR PRADESH

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda has deputed his lieutenant, Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim, to resolve the political impasse in Uttar Pradesh. The aim is to facilitate the installation of a Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) led government in Lucknow before Diwali festival. Under a formula mooted by Gowda, any person other than BSP general secretary Mayawati, could be named for the post of chief minister, including Kanshi Ram. The formula also envisages a cabinet post for Mayawati in the Gowda government and a portfolio of her choice.
The Pioneer
STAGE SET FOR MAHAGUJARAT PARTY GOVERNMENT

Gujarat governor Krishnapal Singh invited leaders of the Mahagujarat Janata Party (MJP) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to prove majority before Tuesday evening. The two parties were asked to parade members of legislative assembly at the Raj Bhawan. While the MJP leaders rejoiced, especially because Congress leaders have announced unconditional support to their effort to form the government, the BJP camp was left shocked. The BJP had not expected the Governor to ask them to prove majority, and if they fail do so now, they would be seen as having made tall claims all along.
The Hindustan Times
WORLD BANK WILL REVIEW ALL 88 PROJECTS

The World Bank would undertake a fresh review of all the 88 projects that are being executed in the country with financial assistance from the multilateral funding body. The review would be completed in next 4-6 months which could lead to killing of projects that have not made progress as per the agreed covenants or experiencing substantive cost and time over-run. Sources said the review would be done in close consultation with the finance ministry.
Financial Express
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS' SANCTIONS DOWN 25 PCT

The investment climate in the country is none-too-encouraging. Sanctions by the public financial institutions (FIs) showed a sharp deceleration in April-August this year compared with the corresponding period last year. This is likely to adversely affect new investment and, consequently, industrial output and exports. The latest data reveals sanctions by FIs dropped in this period by as much as 25 percent for the first time in the last five years. In value terms, they were down from 228.48 billion rupees to 170.36 billion rupees.
INFLATION RISES TO 6.45 PCT

The annual rate of inflation rose to 6.45 percent for the week ended October 5 after registering a decline during the previous week. Inflation was placed at 8.1 percent during the corresponding period of the previous year. This is the 80th week in succession that inflation has veered around single-digit levels even as it failed to stretch its below five percent levels to its 24th week.
INFLATIONARY TREND TO DECIDE NEXT CRR CUT

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) will take into account inflationary expectations before announcing the second phase of cuts in the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) in January. Finance ministry sources said if because of any reason the inflationary pressure went out of control, the RBI might postpone further reduction of CRR. On Saturday, RBI had announced two percent reduction in CRR.
OIL MINISTRY TAKES OVER COAL-BASED METHANE PROJECTS

The ministry of petroleum and natural gas has finally wrested the right to award blocks for exploration and production of coal-bed methane (CBM) from the coal ministry. The decision was taken after a three-year long tussle between the two ministries. The government had originally favoured CBM to be a subject matter of the coal ministry since coal mining safety and continued mining were seen to be important factors while producing CBM.
BMW PUTS BRAKES ON CAR PROJECT

German automaker BMW has stalled its car project in India. The company has instead, decided to study market conditions carefully before getting into the proposed car venture with the Hero group. BMW's original plan was to manufacture the 525 tds (diesel) and 528i (petrol) models from the 5-series range. The former is the most popular model in the 5-series range.
Business Standard
FINANCE MINISTER TO REVIEW BANK LENDING POLICIES

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram will hold meetings with top banks and financial institutions on November 8-9 to review bank lending policies as a followup to the credit policy. The meetings will also focus on lending for export, agriculture and priority sectors. Official sources said the credit policy would cap inflation, nudge lending rates down and improve the environment for fresh investments in industrial and agro-based units.
GOVERNMENT PREPARES TO SET UP TARIFFS PANEL

The government is planning to set up a tariff commission, while the proposed expenditure commission is expected to be set up in time for the presentation of next year's Union budget. Official sources said the industry ministry would pilot the tariff commission before the cabinet. The move had initially come in for strong opposition from some sections of finance ministry which feared that it would be usurped by the protectionist lobby within the country.
PSU SELLOFF MANDATE FOR GLOBAL CONSORTIA LIKELY

The crore group of secretaries is in favour of a consortium of six global merchant bankers each to manage the government's divestment in the Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd and Indian Oil Corporation. The move is likely to bring down the individual fees of the shortlisted merchant bankers to less than 20 million rupees. It is estimated that the two issues together would fetch around 11 billion rupees.
The Economic Times
GLOBAL INVESTMENT MAJORS RENEW INTEREST IN CELLULAR
PROJECTS

Leading global investment banks have evinced renewed interest in selectively funding cellular projects in the regional circles. These banks include Deutsche Morgan Greenfell, Goldman Sachs, Merrill Lynch, SC Warburg, Morgan Stanley and Saloman Brothers. Industry sources said though the bloom was a bit off India lately in terms of international interest in Asian telecommunication, the top banks were once again upbeat on the country's second phase of cellular finance. But, such international assistance would be expected only after the government evolved a security mechanism or offers guarantees to the lendors, sources added.
MOVE TO KEEP REGISTRARS, AGENTS AWAY FROM COMPANIES

The market regulator, Securities & Exchange Board of India (SEBI), is proposing to draft regulations to keep corporates away from their registrars and share transfer agents (R&T). This is a direct fallout of a SEBI internal report on the functioning of Reliance Consultancy Services, the R&T agent for the Reliance group. SEBI sources said the proposed regulations would stipulate that R&T agents could not be associated with the company directly or indirectly.
